The second is being a fit person with a lot of overweight friends. It's been shown that overweight people tend to cause others around them to gain weight, vs a fit person making his circle of overweight friends fit. I probably sound like a total nut job (I am), so I'll just say this:

I agree with that to a degree. Certainly at the end of the day, it all comes down to personal responsibility but at the same time people's lives and choices are influenced by societal factors. Over the past couple of decades, it isn't as if millions of Americans just randomly decided "Hey I know! I'll be a big fat person!" Whatever the factors are (I place most of the blame on the food industry cramming sugar in everything, particularly stuff marketed to kids) it is evident that there were changes to the system and to society that lead to the increase in obesity. At the individual level, sure, any particular person should be able to better educate themselves and get motivated but when that outcome is being socially facilitated on a larger scale, then you'd probably get more results.

Similarly, I totally acknowledge that white people are vastly privileged compared to black people statistically. The problem is it totally breaks down at the individual level. You never know what a particular person's background is or the bullshit they've been through in their life. You don't know if it outweighs yours. Further, it shouldn't matter. In the conversations about ways people should be with each other and what it means to be decent to each other, everyone should have a voice. It's not a zero sum game. I don't have to shut up so you can talk. You can talk and I can talk.

There are so many tools to help people achieve success today that it's almost mind numbing. The Internet gives people access to an infinite amount of information, public libraries are available, grants and scholarships can help make college affordable, the list goes on.

I'm not trying to look like that guy whose response to a beggar is "get a job", because I don't know everyone's personal struggles and I can't make a blanket statement for any particular group because of that.

What I AM trying to say is that in the 21st century, the tools available to help all people in this country succeed have never been more plentiful, and rather than hold individuals accountable for their own actions, many in the SJW camp want to simplify the problem by condemning an entire group based on something they never had any control over (privilege, white guilt, etc).
